persona.generation_guidance: Generate 10-14 personas with deliberately different evaluation habits. Keep only 20-25% of personas as anecdote-carriers; the rest should mainly use math, fee logic, perk usage, approval-denial datapoints, or policy/fine-print corrections. Split the cast across at least five recurring viewpoints: annual-fee skeptics, perk maximizers, math-checkers, customer-service grievance carriers, and cautious questioners. Each persona must have one distinctive hook, one repeated bias, one preferred evidence mode, and one concrete anchor token such as an issuer, benefit, merchant, airport, month, or dollar amount. At least 35-40% of personas should be data-only rather than story-driven. If a persona has an anecdote, keep it to one short incident only; do not give multiple life stories to the same persona. Keep only 15-20% of personas reply-prone, and only when they see a visible numeric claim, denial/approval datapoint, or strong verdict. Allow about 8-10% of personas to sound mildly blunt or irritated, but forbid threats, slurs, identity attacks, or extreme profanity. Avoid generic helpful clones, duplicated anecdote skeletons, and threads where all personas sound equally informed or equally polite.
prompt.comment_style_guidance: Before writing, check the top visible angles and avoid restating the same claim in the same evidence mode. If a draft overlaps too much with a visible comment, switch to a different mode: short calculation, policy/fine-print correction, focused question, skeptical counterexample, or one brief lived datapoint. Thread-level length mix: about 20% one-liners, 35% short comments of 1-2 sentences, 30% medium comments of 2-4 sentences, and 15% longer comments. Keep personal anecdotes to roughly 15-20% of comments, and when used they should be only 1-2 sentences, concrete, and not end with a moralizing lesson line. Prefer more data-only and correction-style comments than story-heavy comments. Keep reply chains selective rather than automatic: most comments should be top-level or shallow replies, and only a minority should continue a back-and-forth. A reply should happen only when the parent includes a clear numeric claim, a denial/approval datapoint, or a strong overconfident verdict. Reply templates should vary across: concise math check, policy correction, one concrete counterexample, or one sharply focused question. Allow rare mild frustration words like ridiculous, annoying, brutal, or absurd in a small minority of comments, but keep the language non-abusive and never threatening. Every comment should add one fresh product-specific detail instead of paraphrasing the thread consensus.
